correctness.rationale: For every smooth Hesse parameter \(\lambda^3\ne-27\), the full cubic Hessian is \(\operatorname{diag}(H_\lambda,6u,6v)\); polar rank at most two is equivalent to an Eckardt point. The determinant identity \(\det H_\lambda=-6\lambda^2 A_\lambda+8(\lambda^3+27)xyz\) proves exactly nine flex lifts; three tail-only points are immediate. The remaining support cases require \(\operatorname{rank}H_\lambda\le1\). Direct rank-one classification yields three base points exactly at \(\lambda=0\) or \(\lambda^3=216\), and six projectively distinct tail lifts per base point. No case is omitted; the classical Hesse modular formula identifies precisely \(j=0\). Exact symbolic verification in verify_hesse.py checks the critical polynomial relations and representative rank calculations. No inference from finite samples to all parameters is made.

value.rationale: Determining all Eckardt points across the full complex one-modulus Thom–Sebastiani cubic-threefold family is a natural classification of a geometric Fano-surface invariant. The exact \(12\)-versus-\(30\) dichotomy and 18-point jump at the equianharmonic modulus explain nontrivial geometry rather than merely recompute the Fermat endpoint or one numerical example; the complete rank-one Hessian locus supports further study of threefold automorphisms and degenerations.
